subject: Startups
title: Due Diligence: What VCs Look For
description: A fast breakdown of Due Diligence: What VCs Look For for builders.

hook.text: Before writing a check, VCs dig deep. Due diligence can take weeks and kill promising deals.

buildup.text: They check financials, talk to customers, call references, and verify every claim the founder made.

discovery.text: The most revealing step: back-channel references. VCs call people the founder didn't list to get honest opinions.

twist.text: Some VCs skip due diligence entirely for hot deals—writing checks in 24 hours to beat competing offers.

climax.text: Skipping diligence works when you know the founder. When you don't, speed can lead to expensive mistakes.

punchline.text: Trust but verify. Or move fast and pray.

quiz.question: What is a back-channel reference in VC due diligence?
options: Calling people the founder didn't list as references
